what: B-roll relevance: lexical (BRL-1) vs visual (SigLIP base int8, K-18) cutaway choice on benchmark narration
machine: shared, noisy 4-vCPU cloud container, no GPU
narration: interview + explainer benchmarks (public-domain NASA): the first 14 non-interviewer sentences of each that are >= 3 s long and have >= 2 concrete terms (28 opportunities); each placed as a 6 s clip after a 5 s opening clip
candidates: NASA Image and Video Library search results for the sentence terms (Openverse excluded: it timed out in this container); visual mode also offered 7 low-speech shots of the local 'broll' and 'documentary' benchmarks (none was chosen)
labelling: one person-equivalent pass by the agent, looking at each chosen picture next to its sentence on the contact sheets in this folder. R = the picture shows the subject or setting the sentence talks about; P = on the programme's topic and plausible as a cutaway but not the specific thing said (e.g. a temperature map for a sentence about temperatures in the tropopause); N = unrelated, a text slate, a talking head, or the source video itself. Not blind, single labeller: treat as indicative.

N_examples: Soyuz crew portrait for cave training
black text slate for 'analog to space'
Mars terrain for 'ozone layer absorbs UV'
a press-release text slate for 'we arrived there around September 11th'
R_examples: lunar pits for 'caves help you prepare to go to the moon'
atmosphere limb from orbit for 'atmosphere is divided into layers'
solar energetic particle diagram for 'the sun's radiation'

first_visual_run_before_the_not_broll_ga.fix: pictures that read as 'a person talking to the camera' / 'people in a television studio' / 'a slide of text' better than the spoken text are rejected (NOT_BROLL)

cost: visual ranking embeds every candidate preview once (~0.2 s each on 2 threads, cached) and each sentence (~0.09 s)
